description_full: Radiant Logistics, Inc., operates as a third-party logistics company, provides technology-enabled global transportation and value-added logistics services in the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The company offers domestic and international air and ocean freight forwarding, and freight brokerage services, including truckload, less-than-truckload (LTL), and intermodal. It also provides other value-added logistics services including materials management and distribution, customs house brokerage, global trade management, and related technology services, as well as arranging shipments, and heavyweight and small package air services. The company serves consumer goods, food and beverages, electronics, high-tech, aviation, automotive, military, government, manufacturing, and retail industries. The company was formerly known as Golf Two Inc. and changed its name to Radiant Logistics, Inc. in October 2005. Radiant Logistics, Inc. was incorporated in 2001 and is headquartered in Renton, Washington.

financial_summary: Radiant Logistics, Inc. is a small-cap industrials business with a $418M market cap on $934M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -5% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 26%.

The business throws off $13M in free cash flow — roughly 1 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.93× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 10.6×.

Shareholder yield is only 0.8%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 24% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
